{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-k2eh","title":"[review] project-LICHEN-2auf.44.7.1: AnnounceState last_relay_map has unbounded growth (memory/DoS)","description":"## Location
`rust/lichen-rpl/src/routing.rs` — `AnnounceState` struct, `should_relay()` method

## Problem
`AnnounceState::should_relay()` inserts every new `originator_iid` (8-byte key) into `last_relay_map: HashMap<[u8; 8], u16>`. There is no eviction policy or maximum capacity.

Each entry consumes ~40-80 bytes (HashMap overhead + key + value). On mesh networks with many nodes or under attack, this grows without bound.

## Impact
- On constrained devices (LICHEN targets STM32WL with 64KB RAM), fragmented heap growth from large HashMaps can cause allocation failure or premature OOM.
- An attacker flooding with unique IIDs can exhaust memory — DoS vector.
- Even in normal operation on a 100+ node mesh, the map grows linearly with node count and never shrinks.

## Fix
Add a maximum capacity (e.g., `MAX_ANNOUNCE_ORIGINATORS: usize = 128`) with LRU or FIFO eviction in `should_relay()`. Alternatively, use a fixed-size `heapless` collection for no_std compatibility.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"agent@lichen-project.dev","created_at":"2026-07-24T16:57:12.560758987Z","created_by":"AI Agent","updated_at":"2026-07-24T16:57:12.560758987Z"}
